shots.title: Leaving Home: packing, pride, Mum’s worry and Keen’s borrowed courage
shots.purpose: At the pier, Keen over-organizes his supplies while insisting he has everything under control; Mum names the size of the step, and Keen looks to the water, swallows, and borrows grown-up words about growing up. This stays one full 30-second emotional-continuity unit so the pier, boat, cargo, Mum and Keen remain alive in the same geography, with enough time for packing business, Mum’s restrained worry and Keen’s final courage line to breathe.
shots.visualPayoff: Keen packs/checks the boat, Mum gently sees through him, and the unit lands wide enough to keep the loaded boat, pier, Mum and Keen readable.
shots.storyBeat: At the pier, Keen over-organizes his supplies while insisting he has everything under control; Mum names the size of the step, and Keen looks to the water, swallows, and borrows grown-up words about growing up. This stays one full 30-second emotional-continuity unit so the pier, boat, cargo, Mum and Keen remain alive in the same geography.
shots.emotionalIntent: Let the ordinary packing become the goodbye; courage must have a visible gulp before it can mean anything.
shots.kidRead: Keen packs carefully, says he is ready, then looks at the water and tries to be brave.
shots.adultRead: A child performs independence while a parent sees the fear underneath and chooses tenderness instead of control.
shots.action: The small sailboat stays moored on the screen-right side of the wooden pier. Keen loads and rechecks the same cargo: open satchel, rolled blanket, folded map and small food pouch. He arranges them carefully, rearranges them, pats the satchel, checks one more pocket, then looks out at the water and swallows. Mum stays beside him on the pier, proud and glassy-eyed, close enough to reassure but not taking over. End wide enough to preserve the pier, sailboat, cargo, Mum and Keen for the next unit.

shots.title: Mum reveals the vacant wristbands, entrusts Keen with his father’s memory, and asks for his promise
shots.purpose: Mum reveals the worn, vacant wristbands, names Keen’s father, lets her private grief surface, then places the bands into Keen’s paws and asks for his promise. Keen receives both the object and its meaning before answering.
shots.visualPayoff: The vacant wristbands pass from Mum’s careful hands into Keen’s paws, and his quiet promise completes the inheritance.
shots.storyBeat: Mum brings out the worn, vacant wristbands and the pier quiets around them. She names Keen’s father and admits that she still feels him every day. Only after Keen has absorbed that truth does she place the bands into his paws, ask for his promise, and receive it.
shots.emotionalIntent: Play one unbroken movement from sacred reveal to inherited responsibility. The emotion lives in careful hands, eye contact, silence and restraint; nothing glows, and nobody rushes the promise.
shots.kidRead: Keen’s Mum gives him his dad’s special wristbands, and Keen promises to wear them.
shots.adultRead: A parent transfers grief, memory and responsibility into her child’s hands, then asks him to carry them forward.
shots.action: Keen pauses beside the already-loaded boat as Mum’s softness turns deliberate. The already-established open satchel remains visible among the boat cargo. Mum lifts the folded map enough to reveal the satchel opening, reaches fully inside, and physically removes exactly two matching vacant gold open cuffs. Keep the satchel, her reaching paw, and both cuffs visible in one continuous cause-and-effect chain so nothing appears from nowhere. Each cuff fits entirely within Mum’s palm; its inner opening is only slightly wider than Keen’s wrist and its rear gap permits it to pass over his paw later. She holds both cuffs carefully between them. Keen becomes completely still. Mum names his father, then admits she still feels him every day. Let the breeze and pier ropes occupy the silence while Keen looks from Mum to the cuffs and understands. Mum places both cuffs gently into Keen’s open paws. He turns them over, feels their physical and emotional weight, and looks back to Mum. She asks for his promise. Keen answers only after the meaning has landed. End with the vacant cuffs in Keen’s paws, his wrists still bare, and their eye contact sustained.

shots.title: Mum and Keen complete their goodbye; Keen pushes off and covers his first wobble
shots.purpose: Carry the emotional goodbye through its physical consequence without a cold cut: Mum gives Keen a portable sense of home, Keen answers with love, then climbs into the boat and leaves. His first wobble releases the ache with character comedy without undoing Mum's tear.
shots.visualPayoff: After the held cheek-touch and goodbye, Keen pushes away from the pier, wobbles, recovers and performs confidence for Mum: 'Still got it!'
shots.storyBeat: With both vacant cuffs already fitted, Mum's touch turns inheritance into belonging. Their goodbye is allowed to land before Keen boards the loaded sailboat, pushes off, waves, wobbles and converts embarrassment into a tiny captain's boast.
shots.emotionalIntent: One continuous emotional exhale from love and ache into departure and a small laugh. The comedy releases the goodbye; it never erases it.
shots.kidRead: Mum and Keen say they love each other, then Keen sails away and pretends his wobble was deliberate.
shots.adultRead: The parent gives the child a portable home and then actually lets him leave; his comic cover-up is the first brave performance she watches from shore.
shots.action: Continue directly from the approved final frame of 3.B3.S1. Both vacant gold cuffs are already fitted, one on each wrist; do not repeat or restage the fitting. Keen turns both wrists once, looks from the blank settings to Mum, and leans into her gentle cheek-touch for one breath. They meet each other's eyes and exchange the goodbye lines without rushing. Hold Mum's final 'my brave boy' in their shared look before either character moves. Then Keen turns toward the already-loaded sailboat, climbs aboard, unties the same mooring rope and pushes away from the same pier. Mum lifts one paw; Keen waves back. As the boat gains a little water between them it wobbles unexpectedly. Keen flails once, catches himself, checks that Mum saw, straightens into borrowed captain confidence and delivers 'Still got it!' Mum's laugh comes through the tear. End with the boat moving cleanly away, Mum still visible on the pier, cargo unchanged, and both empty cuffs visible on Keen's wrists.

shots.title: Squeaky turns the farewell into first adventure as Keen sails toward open water
shots.purpose: Let the world answer Mum's letting-go with a new companion: Squeaky's arrival turns Keen's startle into delight, then the boat carries that warmth into the bittersweet final image of Keen facing open water.
shots.visualPayoff: Squeaky keeps pace beside the sailboat while the pier and Mum grow smaller behind Keen; Keen turns forward carrying nerves and excitement together.
shots.storyBeat: Mum laughs through a tear, then Squeaky bursts beside the moving boat and becomes Keen's first companion beyond home. Their playful exchange flows into the widening distance from the pier, ending with Keen looking ahead: a little nervous, a little excited, a lot of both.
shots.emotionalIntent: Let play rush in like sunlight after the ache, then leave a bittersweet wake rather than resetting the emotion. Mum remains visible until distance, not a cut, carries her away.
shots.kidRead: A friendly dolphin joins Keen, and together they sail toward an adventure.
shots.adultRead: The world answers the parent's release with companionship; home recedes without disappearing from the child.
shots.action: Continue from 3.B5.S1 with the same sailboat already moving away from the same pier, the same cargo secured, Mum behind Keen and both vacant cuffs still on his wrists. Mum laughs through her tear. A sudden splash erupts beside the hull and exactly one Squeaky rises from the water. Keen startles, then lights up. Squeaky chirps and makes one clean playful leap; Keen leans safely over the side, answers him, and nods as if he understands every chirp. Keep the boat progressing throughout: near water moves fastest, the pier and Mum drift smaller behind, and open blue water grows ahead. After their final exchange, Squeaky keeps pace beside the hull. Keen looks back once toward Mum, then turns forward. Let delight settle into a truthful mixture of nerves and excitement. End with Keen and Squeaky moving toward open water, Mum still readable but small on the distant pier, both cuffs vacant and unchanged, and the original island geography receding behind them.

promptContract.prompt:
[Opening Stage]
Playable 16:9 anticipation for 3.B1.S1; no portrait or payoff.

[References]
- Project-stable slots: @图1=Keen; @图2=Keen's Mum; @图3=scene plate. Never swap roles.
- Multi-angle collapse: @图1=one Keen; @图2=one Keen's Mum; views are angles, not extra characters.
- @图1: Keen turnaround; exact identity/proportions only; ignore background/pose.
- @图2: Keen's Mum turnaround; exact identity/proportions only; ignore background/pose.
- @图3: approved Scene Look; world, scale, materials, light and atmosphere only.
- Keep identities distinct; no blending.

[Characters In Frame]
- Keen
- Keen's Mum

[Intended Read]
A tactile pier goodbye: Keen is actively checking and loading his departure supplies into the little sailboat while trying to look ready; Mum stands nearby, proud and worried, giving him room to be brave.

[Scene Look]
@图3 is the approved visual authority for world, canonical style, materials, light and atmosphere.

[Geography]
Screen-right is open water; the small sailboat is moored alongside the right edge of the dock with its cockpit/open storage visible to camera.
Screen-left is the shoreward side with sand, posts, rope and dense island greenery behind.
The dock planks run from lower foreground toward the sailboat, creating a clear packing-and-departure axis.
Keen is beside the sailboat gunwale/cockpit with both hands on or reaching into the travel supplies.
Keen's Mum stands screen-left of Keen on the same dock depth plane, facing his working space and giving him room.
Keep the satchel, rolled blanket, folded map and small food pouch unobstructed and readable as the main frame story.

[Frame]
- Keen @ lower-centre area; active opening frame: leaning or crouched at the sailboat edge with both hands on an open satchel and rolled blanket inside the boat, checking the packed items; facing three-quarter toward the open sailboat cockpit and travel supplies at frame-right, with slight awareness back toward Mum.
- Keen's Mum @ lower-left area; supportive parental stillness, proud and worried, standing screen-left and leaving Keen room to load/check the boat; facing three-quarter toward Keen and the boat supplies.
- Same depth: Keen 57 inches; Keen's Mum 60 inches; preserve relative-size truth only.

[Negative Space]
Lead room stays open frame-right for the approved direction of travel.
Hold open working space around Keen's paws, the boat gunwale and the supplies so the loading/checking action reads immediately.
Keep a clear empty corridor between Keen and Keen's Mum so their goodbye space remains readable.
Reserve the foreground/midground around the satchel, rolled blanket, folded map and food pouch; do not cover them with ropes, posts or clutter.
Leave open sea and sky beyond the boat so the departure direction remains clear.

[Camera]
Low, intimate wide-medium camera at roughly child chest-to-eye height, about a 32–35mm animated-feature lens relationship: close enough to feel tactile wood, rope and supplies.

[Performance Freedom]
Animation owns later performance and motion.

[Protect]
Exactly one Keen and one Keen's Mum appear in this image.
Keep Keen and Keen's Mum at the same distance from the camera; Keen's Mum appears about 5% taller than Keen.
Keen starts this scene with bare wrists: no wristbands, bands, bracelets, cuffs, crystals, straps or wrist accessories on either wrist.
Include only the characters listed in charactersInFrame: Keen and Keen's Mum.
Maintain canon relative scale: Keen is 57 inches, Keen's Mum is 60 inches; they share the same depth plane with no perspective size cheat.
Do not stage a passive standing pose; Keen must be visibly loading or checking the boat supplies in the opening keyframe.
No crystal-like baskets, ceremonial loads, glowing stones or aquamarine crystals appear in this shot.

[Forbidden]
No portrait/payoff, identity or scale drift, altered reference features, duplicates, anatomy errors, extra cast/props, text, watermarks or body-mounted loads.

output.generationGoal: Create a 30-second emotional-continuity unit at the pier where Keen over-organizes the boat supplies, reassures Mum, then finds visible courage by meeting her eyes before facing the open water.
output.deliveryPlan: Use three broad timestamp stages inside one continuous geography: practical packing as emotional cover, Mum’s contained worry as pressure, then Keen’s water-facing gulp, direct eye contact with Mum on ‘Like you said’, visible reception of her quiet reassurance, and return to the horizon for the held courage line; keep @Audio1 authoritative and let the camera breathe wider at the end for the next unit.

interpretation.jokeOrAche: The ache is a child performing readiness through over-checking while his mother sees both the bravery and the fear underneath.
interpretation.mechanism: Small practical actions carry the goodbye: repeated packing looks efficient at first, then reveals nerves; Mum’s restraint makes the ordinary dock business emotionally charged.
interpretation.statusBefore: Keen appears busy and in control beside the moored boat, with Mum close enough to help but choosing not to take over.
interpretation.statusAfter: Keen still looks young, but direct eye contact lets him visibly borrow Mum’s courage before he faces the water while she lets the step happen.
audienceProgression: We first read Keen’s careful packing as readiness and competence.
We then notice the repeated checks are really a way to manage fear while Mum quietly understands.
We end feeling that courage is not certainty; it is the visible gulp, the look to Mum that asks for strength, and the choice to face the water anyway.
interpretation.emotionalHeart: A parent and child both practice letting go without saying goodbye too directly.

generationDesign.densityJudgement: Emotional-continuity rather than physical-comedy density: one pier geography, one cargo business thread, four locked audio beats and one final courage hold fit as a single 30-second unit.
generationDesign.splitOrNonSplitRationale: Splitting would weaken the goodbye because the packing, Mum’s worry and Keen’s courage all depend on the same live relationship to the boat, pier and water.
generationDesign.handoffState: Keen packs/checks the boat, Mum gently sees through him, and the unit lands wide enough to keep the loaded boat, pier, Mum and Keen readable.

output.dramaticBeat: At the pier, Keen over-organizes his supplies while insisting he has everything under control; Mum names the size of the step, and Keen looks to the water, swallows, meets her eyes to borrow courage, then turns back to the horizon and speaks about growing up.
output.audienceBefore: The audience expects a simple departure-prep moment and sees Keen trying to be official.
output.audienceAfter: The audience understands the packing was the goodbye and feels courage pass silently from Mum to Keen before he faces the water.
output.beatOwner: Keen owns the visible action and final courage; Keen’s Mum owns the emotional truth that exposes the size of the step.
output.performanceFreedom: Seedance may discover natural hand hesitations, eye travel, breath timing, secondary fur and sail motion, and organic camera drift, provided the cargo, geography, bare wrists, audio authority and final held relationship remain intact.
output.performanceArc: Keen moves from busy control, to tidy performed confidence, to a quiet gulp toward the water; on ‘Like you said’ he turns and meets Mum’s eyes, visibly receives her still reassurance, then carries that borrowed courage back toward the horizon. Mum moves from proud restraint, to exposed worry, to loving acceptance communicated through sustained eye contact without taking over.

Keen over-organizes the final supplies in his little sailboat while his Mum gently checks on him, revealing his performed confidence and her proud, tender worry.

Performance: Keen looks pleased with his system until a pause pulls him into another check; Mum watches screen-left with proud stillness. lines.speaker: Keen's Mum
lines.exactDialogue: Wherever you go… You’ll never be alone.
lines.performedText: [gently] Wherever you go… You’ll never be alone.
lines.dramaticIntention: Give Keen the cuffs as emotional shelter, not instruction; she is placing home inside him before letting him leave.
